name: Board Governance Framework
description: FirstUK Bank's established governance framework that defines Board responsibilities, executive authority, internal controls, and regulatory compliance structure. This framework serves as the foundational policy governing the bank's organizational and risk management structure.
context: Establish FirstUK Bank's governance framework, defining Board responsibilities, executive authority, internal controls, and regulatory compliance structure.

name: Board
description: The governing body of FirstUK Bank responsible for setting strategic direction, overseeing executive authority, and ensuring regulatory compliance. The Board's responsibilities are formally defined within the governance framework.
context: defining Board responsibilities, executive authority, internal controls, and regulatory compliance structure

name: Board
description: The Board of FirstUK Bank provides strategic direction and risk oversight as the primary governance body. It operates under defined authority and accountability frameworks.
context: Board provides strategic direction and risk oversight
Defined responsibilities at each level (Board, Executive, Managers)

name: Risk Committee
description: The Risk Committee provides independent assurance and challenge to the Board on risk management matters at FirstUK Bank.
context: Risk and Audit committees provide independent assurance

name: Audit Committee
description: The Audit Committee provides independent assurance and challenge to the Board on audit and control matters at FirstUK Bank.
context: Risk and Audit committees provide independent assurance

name: FirstUK Bank Governance Framework
description: FirstUK Bank has established a formal governance framework comprising seven core principles: Board Leadership, Clear Authority, Independent Challenge, Transparency, Accountability, Compliance, and Ethics. These principles define the bank's approach to strategic direction, risk oversight, regulatory compliance, and ethical operations.
context: FirstUK Bank operates according to the following governance principles
Board provides strategic direction and risk oversight
Full compliance with FCA, PRA, and legal requirements
High ethical standards in decision-making and operations

name: Board of Directors Composition and Structure
description: The Board of Directors is structured with 5–7 members per FCA guidance, comprising an independent Non-Executive Chair, a sole Executive Director (CEO), and a majority of Independent Non-Executive Directors. The Board maintains a mix of banking, risk, finance, and compliance expertise to support effective governance and risk oversight.
context: CEO: Executive director (sole executive on Board)
Expertise: Mix of banking, risk, finance, compliance expertise

name: Board of Directors
description: The governing body of the bank responsible for strategic oversight, risk governance, and compliance. Comprises 5–7 directors including an independent Non-Executive Chair, the CEO as sole executive, and a majority of Independent Non-Executive Directors with mixed expertise in banking, risk, finance, and compliance.
context: CEO: Executive director (sole executive on Board)

name: Chair
description: The Chair of the Board of Directors, who must be an Independent Non-Executive Director per FCA guidance. Responsible for leading the Board and ensuring effective governance.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: The sole Executive Director on the Board, responsible for executive leadership and operational management of the bank.
context: CEO: Executive director (sole executive on Board)

name: Independent Non-Executive Director
description: Independent Non-Executive Directors form the majority of the Board and provide independent oversight, challenge, and expertise in banking, risk, finance, and compliance matters.
context: Expertise: Mix of banking, risk, finance, compliance expertise

name: Board Approval of Business Strategy
description: Board-level decision to approve the bank's business strategy, establishing the strategic direction and priorities for the organisation.

name: Board Approval of Annual Budget and Capital Plan
description: Board-level decision to approve the annual budget and capital plan, governing financial resource allocation and capital deployment.
context: Approve annual budget and capital plan
Strategic: Approve annual budget and capital plan

name: Board Approval of Material Acquisitions and Disposals
description: Board-level decision to approve material acquisitions and disposals, ensuring strategic alignment and financial prudence in significant transactions.

name: Risk Appetite
description: The board's formal statement and approval of the organisation's risk appetite, defining the level and types of risk the bank is willing to accept in pursuit of its strategic objectives.

name: Board Approval of Policies and Procedures
description: Board-level decision to approve the bank's policies and procedures, establishing the governance framework and operational standards.

name: Board Approval of Committee Charters
description: Board-level decision to approve committee charters, defining the mandate, composition, and responsibilities of board committees.

name: Board Monitoring of Compliance
description: Board-level responsibility to monitor compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies across the organisation.

name: Board Appointment of Executives
description: Board-level decision to appoint senior executives, ensuring appropriate leadership and accountability structures.

name: Board Oversight of Risk Management
description: Board-level responsibility to oversee the bank's risk management framework, ensuring effective identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks.

name: Board Review of Internal Controls
description: Board-level responsibility to review the effectiveness of internal controls, ensuring adequate safeguards over assets and operations.

name: Board Receipt of Audit Reports
description: Board-level responsibility to receive and review internal audit reports, ensuring visibility of audit findings and management responses.

name: Capital Adequacy
description: Board-level monitoring of capital adequacy, ensuring the bank maintains sufficient capital to support its risk profile and regulatory requirements.

name: Board Regulatory Engagement
description: Board-level responsibility for regulatory engagement, maintaining effective communication and compliance with financial regulators.

name: Board Shareholder Communication
description: Board-level responsibility for shareholder communication, ensuring transparent and timely disclosure of material information.

name: Board Public Disclosures
description: Board-level responsibility for public disclosures, ensuring compliance with disclosure obligations and market conduct standards.

name: Board Crisis Management
description: Board-level responsibility for crisis management, ensuring effective response to significant operational, reputational, or regulatory incidents.

name: Board Meeting Governance Framework
description: Formal governance structure establishing quarterly board meetings as the minimum frequency for strategic, governance, risk, and financial decision-making. All directors are expected to attend, with papers provided one week in advance and minutes approved and retained as permanent records.
context: Agenda: Strategic, governance, risk, financial matters

name: Board Risk Committee
description: A board-level committee responsible for overseeing risk strategy, appetite setting, capital adequacy, audit findings review, and regulatory compliance. Meets on a quarterly basis to discharge governance oversight of enterprise risk management.

name: Board Audit Committee
description: A governance committee with quarterly meeting frequency, composed of a majority of independent Non-Executive Directors. Responsible for internal audit oversight, external audit coordination, financial reporting, and control environment assessment.

name: Board Remuneration Committee
description: A board-level committee responsible for overseeing executive compensation, staff incentive schemes, and conflict of interest management. The committee is composed of a majority of independent Non-Executive Directors and meets on a quarterly basis.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: The Chief Executive Officer holds chief executive responsibility for business performance, regulatory interface, and crisis management. Reports directly to the Board with monthly financial performance reports, quarterly risk dashboards, and annual strategy reviews.

name: Board
description: The Board is the governing body to which the Chief Executive Officer reports. It receives monthly financial performance reports, quarterly risk dashboards, and annual strategy reviews.

name: Chief Financial Officer
description: Senior executive responsible for financial management, reporting, treasury, funding, capital management, and investment decisions. Reports directly to the CEO and Board.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive function responsible for enterprise risk management, capital and liquidity management, risk policy approval, and regulatory compliance oversight. Reports functionally to the Board Risk Committee and administratively to the CEO, with structural independence from operational departments.
context: Reports to: Board Risk Committee (functionally), CEO (administratively)

name: Board Risk Committee
description: Governance body to which the Chief Risk Officer reports functionally for enterprise risk management and risk policy matters. Acts as the functional oversight authority for risk governance.
context: Reports to: Board Risk Committee (functionally), CEO (administratively)

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Senior executive role responsible for business operations, process management, operational efficiency, and customer service. Reports directly to the CEO and holds authority over operational functions.
context: Authority: Business operations, Process management, Operational efficiency, Customer service

name: Chief Technology Officer
description: Senior executive responsible for technology strategy, infrastructure management, system availability, security oversight, and cybersecurity governance. Reports directly to the CEO and holds authority over technology investment decisions.

name: Technology Department
description: Organisational function led by the CTO with responsibility for technology strategy, infrastructure, system availability, security, and cybersecurity governance.

name: Chief Information Security Officer
description: Executive role responsible for information security policy, cybersecurity incident response, data protection, privacy, and security risk assessment. Reports functionally to the CTO and to the Board Risk Committee for security risk matters.
context: Reports to: CTO (functionally), Board Risk Committee (for security risk)

name: Chief Technology Officer
description: Executive role to which the CISO reports functionally for information security, cybersecurity, data protection, and security risk assessment matters.
context: Reports to: CTO (functionally), Board Risk Committee (for security risk)

name: Board Risk Committee
description: Governance body to which the CISO reports for security risk matters, providing oversight of cybersecurity incident response and security risk assessment.
context: Reports to: CTO (functionally), Board Risk Committee (for security risk)

name: Cybersecurity Risk
description: Risk category encompassing information security threats, cybersecurity incidents, and data protection vulnerabilities. Managed by the CISO with oversight from the Board Risk Committee.

name: Business Units
description: First line of defense responsible for day-to-day risk management, control execution, and daily monitoring with escalation protocols. Business units own and operate their own controls as the primary defense mechanism.

name: Risk & Compliance
description: Second line of defense providing independent risk oversight, compliance testing, control design review, and key control monitoring. Functions as the independent oversight layer between business operations and internal audit.

name: Internal Audit
description: Third line of defense providing independent assurance through risk-based annual audit planning, finding identification, follow-up tracking, and reporting to the Board Audit Committee. Serves as the ultimate independent verification layer.

name: Board Audit Committee
description: Governance body that receives reports and findings from Internal Audit regarding the three lines of defense framework and control effectiveness. Responsible for oversight of the internal controls framework.

name: Board Risk Committee Charter
description: Formal charter document establishing the mandate, authority, and responsibilities of the Board Risk Committee within the organization's governance framework.

name: Internal Audit Charter
description: Formal charter document defining the scope, authority, reporting lines, and independence of the Internal Audit function within the organization.

name: Internal Audit
description: The internal audit function responsible for independent assessment of the organization's risk management, control, and governance processes.

name: Board Risk Committee
description: Board-level committee responsible for oversight of the organization's risk management framework, risk appetite, and risk governance.

name: Operational Risk Policy
description: A formal policy governing the identification, assessment, and management of operational risks within the organisation. This policy establishes the framework for managing risks arising from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events.

name: Risk Appetite Statement
description: A formal statement defining the organisation's risk appetite and tolerance levels across risk categories for 2026. This document establishes the boundaries within which the bank is willing to operate and the thresholds for escalation and governance oversight.

name: Anti-Money Laundering Policy
description: A formal policy establishing the bank's framework for detecting, preventing, and reporting money laundering and terrorist financing activities. This policy defines AML screening procedures, transaction monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations to relevant authorities.

name: Customer Identification
description: Customer Identification policy establishing Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements for customer onboarding and ongoing compliance. This policy governs the identity verification process as a core compliance obligation.

name: Privacy and Data Protection
description: Privacy and Data Protection policy addressing GDPR compliance requirements. This policy establishes the bank's framework for handling personal data and ensuring regulatory compliance with data protection legislation.

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: Formal policy governing the bank's complaint handling procedures and customer complaint resolution processes. This policy establishes the framework for managing and resolving customer complaints in compliance with regulatory requirements.

name: Escalation Matrix
description: Operational procedures defining escalation pathways and decision authorities for incident handling and governance matters.

name: Incident Response Plan
description: Operational procedures establishing the framework and protocols for detecting, investigating, and responding to operational incidents and security events.

name: Information Security Policy
description: A formal policy governing information security practices and controls within the bank. This policy establishes the framework for protecting information assets and managing security risks across the organisation.

name: Fraud Prevention Policy
description: A formal policy establishing the bank's approach to fraud prevention, detection, and response. This policy defines controls and procedures to mitigate fraud risk across customer accounts and transactions.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Conduct of Business Handbook
description: FCA regulatory handbook section establishing conduct of business requirements for financial institutions. Covers customer treatment, product governance, and market conduct obligations applicable to the bank's operations.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Systems and Controls Handbook
description: FCA regulatory handbook section prescribing systems and controls requirements for financial institutions. Establishes governance, risk management, and operational resilience standards.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Dispute Resolution Handbook
description: FCA regulatory handbook section governing dispute resolution and complaints handling procedures. Establishes requirements for fair and timely resolution of customer complaints.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Supervision Handbook
description: FCA regulatory handbook section covering supervision, reporting, and regulatory engagement requirements. Establishes framework for ongoing regulatory oversight and firm-to-regulator communications.

name: Customer Identification Know Your Customer Process
description: FCA compliance requirement mandating customer identification procedures. Establishes the bank's obligation to verify customer identity as part of financial crime prevention and regulatory compliance.

name: Anti-Money Laundering Screening Program
description: FCA compliance requirement establishing anti-money laundering screening obligations. Encompasses sanctions checks, PEP screening, and transaction monitoring to prevent financial crime.

name: Financial Crime Risk
description: Regulatory compliance risk related to financial crime prevention obligations. Encompasses AML, sanctions, and fraud prevention requirements mandated by FCA framework.

name: Market Conduct Risk
description: Regulatory compliance risk arising from FCA conduct of business requirements. Covers fair treatment of customers and market conduct obligations.

name: Complaints and Dispute Resolution Risk
description: Regulatory compliance risk related to fair treatment and complaints handling obligations. Established under FCA DISP handbook requirements for timely and fair customer dispute resolution.

name: Prudential Regulation Authority Rulebook
description: The PRA Rulebook establishes regulatory requirements across capital adequacy (Pillar 1), risk management (Pillar 2), operational resilience (Pillar 2), and liquidity management. It mandates minimum capital ratios, risk governance frameworks, system availability standards (RTO/RPO), and stress testing obligations for regulated entities.

name: Capital Adequacy Risk
description: Capital adequacy risk as defined under PRA Pillar 1 requirements. The institution must maintain minimum capital ratios to absorb potential losses and support ongoing operations.

name: Operational Resilience Risk
description: Operational resilience risk as mandated under PRA Pillar 2, encompassing system availability, recovery time objectives (RTO), and recovery point objectives (RPO) to ensure business continuity.

name: Liquidity Risk
description: Liquidity management risk as a PRA regulatory requirement. The institution must maintain adequate liquidity to meet obligations and support normal operations under stressed conditions.

name: Risk Management Governance
description: Risk management governance framework mandated under PRA Pillar 2, requiring robust governance structures and processes to identify, measure, monitor, and control risks.

name: Minimum Capital Ratio
description: PRA-mandated minimum capital ratio threshold that regulated institutions must maintain to ensure adequate capital buffers against potential losses.

name: System Availability Target
description: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) metrics mandated under PRA operational resilience requirements to define acceptable system downtime and data loss thresholds.

name: Stress Testing Execution
description: Ongoing compliance obligation to conduct stress testing as mandated by PRA Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 requirements. Stress tests assess the institution's resilience under adverse economic scenarios.

name: Compliance Department
description: Organisational department responsible for regulatory engagement, supervisory contact management, and compliance data reporting to the FCA/PRA. Manages quarterly meetings with supervisory teams and annual reporting obligations.

name: FCA Supervisory Engagement
description: Ongoing regulatory engagement with the Financial Conduct Authority through designated supervisory contact, quarterly meetings, and annual compliance reporting requirements.
context: Annual Reporting: Compliance data to FCA

name: PRA Supervisory Engagement
description: Ongoing regulatory engagement with the Prudential Regulation Authority through designated supervisory contact and quarterly meetings with supervisory team.

name: Quarterly Supervisory Meetings
description: Recurring compliance monitoring activity involving meetings with the FCA/PRA supervisory team on a quarterly basis to discuss regulatory matters and compliance status.

name: Annual Compliance Data Reporting to FCA
description: Annual regulatory reporting obligation requiring submission of compliance data to the FCA as part of supervisory engagement and regulatory oversight.
context: Annual Reporting: Compliance data to FCA

name: Voluntary Breach Self-Disclosure
description: Compliance process for voluntary reporting of breaches to regulatory authorities, supporting transparent regulatory engagement and breach management.

name: Compliance Risk
description: Compliance risk is monitored through a structured internal monitoring framework with monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual review cycles. The monitoring includes dashboard metrics, risk committee reviews, control testing, and full governance assessments.

name: Operational Risk
description: Operational risk is subject to ongoing internal monitoring through a tiered review schedule encompassing monthly compliance dashboards, quarterly risk committee assessments, semi-annual control testing, and annual full governance reviews.

name: Quarterly Risk Committee Review
description: A formal quarterly governance review conducted by the risk committee to assess compliance and operational risk metrics, control effectiveness, and governance alignment.

name: Annual Full Governance Review
description: An annual comprehensive governance review that encompasses all monitoring activities, control testing results, and risk assessments to ensure organizational compliance and risk management effectiveness.

name: Compliance Dashboard Key Metrics
description: Monthly compliance dashboard tracking key performance indicators and compliance metrics as part of the internal monitoring framework.

name: Semi-Annual Control Testing
description: Semi-annual control testing conducted as part of the internal audit function to assess the effectiveness of operational and compliance controls across the organization.

name: Risk Committee
description: The risk committee is responsible for quarterly reviews of compliance and operational risk metrics, control effectiveness, and governance alignment as part of the internal monitoring framework.

name: Internal Audit
description: The internal audit function responsible for executing the annual audit plan and providing quarterly reporting to governance bodies on audit findings and risk assessments.
context: Internal Audit: Annual audit plan, quarterly reporting

name: External Audit
description: The external audit function responsible for conducting the annual financial audit of the bank's financial statements and controls.

name: Regulatory Audit
description: The regulatory audit function encompassing periodic examinations conducted by the FCA and PRA to assess compliance with regulatory requirements and prudential standards.

name: Annual Audit Plan Execution
description: The annual audit plan that defines the scope, timing, and resource allocation for internal audit activities across the bank's key risk areas and processes.

name: Quarterly Audit Reporting
description: The quarterly reporting obligation of the Internal Audit function to provide governance bodies with updates on audit findings, remediation status, and emerging risks.

name: Annual Financial Audit
description: The annual financial audit conducted by external auditors to provide independent assurance over the bank's financial statements and the effectiveness of internal controls.

name: FCA/PRA Periodic Examinations
description: Periodic examinations conducted by the FCA and PRA to assess the bank's compliance with regulatory requirements, prudential standards, and governance frameworks.

name: Conflict of Interest Policy
description: A formal policy requiring all staff and directors to declare conflicts of interest, with annual minimum review cycles, escalation procedures for conflicts that arise, and transaction restrictions where appropriate.

name: Conflict of Interest Declaration
description: A mandatory declaration requirement applicable to all staff and directors as part of the Conflict of Interest Policy framework.

name: Annual Conflict of Interest Policy Review
description: A recurring governance action requiring regular review of the Conflict of Interest Policy at a minimum annual frequency to ensure continued effectiveness and relevance.

name: Conflict of Interest Escalation Procedure
description: A defined escalation procedure to be invoked when a conflict of interest arises, ensuring appropriate governance oversight and resolution.

name: Staff
description: All bank staff members subject to the Conflict of Interest Policy declaration and review requirements.

name: Directors
description: Board directors subject to the Conflict of Interest Policy declaration and review requirements.

name: Ethics Standards Framework
description: A formal governance framework establishing that all decisions must be made in the customer's best interest, with no conflicts of interest permitted to override customer interests. The framework mandates transparency in communications and fair dealing with all stakeholders.
context: All decisions made in customer's best interest

name: Compliance Department
description: Department responsible for ensuring regulatory compliance and managing compliance data reporting to regulators.
context: Regulatory Reports: Compliance data, capital ratios

name: Risk Department
description: Department responsible for capital ratio management and risk-related regulatory reporting.
context: Regulatory Reports: Compliance data, capital ratios

name: Capital Adequacy Risk
description: Risk related to maintaining adequate capital ratios as reported to regulators and disclosed in regulatory reports.
context: Regulatory Reports: Compliance data, capital ratios

name: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Risk of non-compliance with regulatory changes and requirements communicated through regulatory circulars and updates.
context: Regulatory Circulars: Updates on regulatory changes

name: Reputational Risk
description: Risk to bank reputation arising from unfair, non-transparent, or untimely customer communications.

name: Regulatory Circulars
description: Updates on regulatory changes issued by regulatory authorities that require bank action and awareness.
context: Regulatory Circulars: Updates on regulatory changes

name: Customer
description: Bank customers who receive fair, transparent, and timely communications regarding their accounts and banking services.

name: Board Report
description: Quarterly formal report to the Board covering financial performance, risk posture, and governance matters. Serves as a key governance communication mechanism for board-level oversight and decision-making.

name: Operational Risk
description: Operational risk exposure tracked and reported monthly through the Risk Dashboard. Covers process failures, system outages, and control deficiencies across the organisation.

name: Compliance Risk
description: Compliance risk exposure monitored and reported monthly through the Risk Dashboard. Encompasses regulatory breaches, policy violations, and control failures.

name: Fraud Risk
description: Fraud risk exposure tracked and reported monthly through the Risk Dashboard. Includes detection, investigation, and prevention of fraudulent activities across customer accounts and transactions.

name: Quarterly Audit Report
description: Quarterly internal audit report documenting audit findings and follow-up actions on previously identified issues. Provides formal assessment of control effectiveness and compliance posture.

name: Staff Policy and Training Communications
description: Regular communications to all staff covering policy updates, procedural changes, and mandatory training requirements. Ensures organisation-wide awareness and compliance with governance and risk management standards.
